messages:
eric (sec): Quick heads-up — NVIDIA released a security fix that maps to CVE-2026-0456 affecting the kernel interface for NV driver signing. We need to decide prioritization and canary strategy. Any blocking compatibility concerns with our CUDA/cuDNN/NCCL matrix?

Tanvi (eng-infra): Do we have the vendor package hash/KMS-signed artifact yet? If it's signed with our KMS flow we can validate signature in CI before pushing. Also need kernel ABI list (4.19, 5.10, 5.15) smoke coverage.

Olivia (eng-ml): From model infra POV, main risk is KV cache invalidation during driver module reloads. If the update forces a reboot of long-lived serving nodes we need migration windows. Which drivers versions are targeted? cuDNN API compatibility matters for fp16 ops.

Dylan (sre): Proposed canary plan: 2 nodes in eu-west-1, 2 nodes in us-west-2 with identical workloads (chatgen small-ish batch). Steps: 1) verify KMS signature locally, 2) install to canary with live traffic diverted (10% traffic), 3) run smoke tests (see list below), 4) monitor 15m for kernel oops, timeouts, OOMs, and throughput regressions. Rollback = apt rollback + node drain -> replace.

Jenna (eng-runtime): Smoke tests (quick):
```
# driver smoke
modinfo nvidia | head -n 5
nvidia-smi -q | grep "Driver Version"
docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi
# basic perf test
python perf/check_latency.py --model llama-2-7b --batch 1 --tokens 64
```
Also: run a short cuDNN conv test and a NCCL allreduce micro-benchmark.

Tanvi (eng-infra): KMS notes: we must confirm HSM signing key ID and include verification step in preflight. I can add a CI job that runs `kms verify-sig --key=redwood-nv --artifact driver.tgz.sig driver.tgz` and fails build on mismatch.

eric (sec): Good. Also need an audit trail: who triggered the rollout, sig verification record, and RBAC check (only release engineers + infra can push signed drivers). Can we gate the canary deploy behind an RBAC check in console?

Dylan (sre): Yes — we can require a signed release token from the release pipeline. For quick ops we can annotate the deploy with `release=nv-cve-0456` and record the operator in audit logs. I’ll add a one-click rollback script to the runbook.

Olivia (eng-ml): Compatibility matrix quick checklist: CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9.0, NCCL 2.17. If driver < 535.x we might see slow kernels. I’ll run a smoke run against the canary nodes once they’re up.

ci-bot: artifact signed: driver-535.86.01.tgz.sig verified by kms:redwood-nv at 1908801280 UTC.

Jenna (eng-runtime): Note: if we hit kernel module tainting or symbol version mismatches we should NOT attempt hot-reload on production. Plan for node replacement. Add a preflight that checks `dmesg | tail -n 50` for WARN/ERR after install.

eric (sec): Action items: 1) Tanvi add KMS verification job + RBAC gating (due EOD), 2) Dylan create canary pool and automated rollback script (start now), 3) Jenna add smoke scripts to repo and CI hook, 4) Olivia run perf compatibility checks on canaries once live. We’ll reconvene after 30m of canary traffic or earlier if any fail. :thumbsup:

Dylan (sre): Starting canary deploy now — will ping with status.

ci-bot: canary deploy started for release nv-cve-0456 on 1908801332.

Dylan (sre): Canary update — cpu spikes observed on one pod, scaling to 2 replicas resolved it. No kernel oops so far (monitoring).

eric (sec): Keep audit entries and attach signature verification logs to the incident ticket. If anything odd, isolate node and dump /var/log/messages and dmesg.

(ended)
